name: Iceland
summary_text: Iceland is one of the safest countries in the world for transgender visitors. The 2019 Gender Autonomy Act allows self-defined gender registration without diagnosis or surgery, non-binary people can use an "X" marker, and discrimination on grounds of gender identity and expression is banned in services and employment. General crime rates are very low. Local travel businesses actively accommodate trans visitors: a dedicated traveller guide from Pink Iceland reports that most Reykjavík-area swimming pools offer private or gender-neutral changing rooms, that using binary changing rooms is legal and common, and that trans visitors generally "shouldn't have to be worried about your safety". Emergency services maintain dedicated guidance for queer victims of abuse and hate crime. Residual risks are small: potential hate-crime reports have risen in recent years (from very low absolute levels), Iceland's hate-crime law works through sentencing aggravation rather than a standalone offence, and occasional misgendering — usually unintentional — still occurs.

sources.claim_summary: Pink Iceland travel information for trans and non-binary travellers (updated 2025): since 2019, informed-consent healthcare and name/gender change via the National Registry without medical diagnosis (under-18s with parental consent); social attitudes accepting; low crime; most capital-area swimming pools offer private, gender-neutral locker rooms usable without questions.

sources.title: Iceland | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): marriage and adoption; employment discrimination banned on SOGIESC grounds since 2018; self-determination gender markers and 'X' documents; intersex surgeries on minors banned in most cases; a conversion-practices ban with criminal penalties took effect January 2024; high public acceptance; Pride parades with several thousand attendees and government participation.

Equaldex data for Iceland: homosexuality legal, marriage legal, gender change with no restrictions, nonbinary recognised, hate-crime protections cover SOGI, discrimination illegal, full ban on intersex infant surgery, conversion therapy banned, bathroom access protected. Ranked #1 of 121 regions for 'good place' for gay and lesbian people (93%).
OSCE/ODIHR page on Iceland's hate-crime legislation: General Penal Code Article 70 lists gender characteristics, sexuality and gender identity among aggravating factors when deciding punishment.

sources.title: National frameworks to address hate crime in Iceland | HCRW
sources.claim_summary: OSCE/ODIHR page on Iceland's national hate-crime frameworks: data collected by the National Police Commissioner include discrimination and defamation cases; no systematic collection of hate-crime statistics.

sources.title: Hate crimes
sources.claim_summary: Iceland's 112 emergency service information page on hate crime: the term 'hate crime' does not appear in Icelandic law, but victim status (including gender identity and sexual characteristics) must be considered in sentencing under General Penal Code Article 70; explains hate speech and discrimination definitions.

sources.title: Abuse against queer people
sources.claim_summary: 112.is information page on abuse against queer people in Iceland: queer people are more likely to be victims of violence; marginalisation, fear of isolation, and barriers to seeking help; all public services available to victims.

sources.title: Queer Rights Group Calls for Stronger Hate Crime Legislation
sources.claim_summary: Iceland Review (Aug 2025): potential hate crimes recorded by police have risen - 16 cases in 2023 (triple the prior year), 11 in 2024, 7 so far in 2025; Samtökin '78 (national queer organisation) says cases linked to gender identity have become more common since 2018 and calls for stronger hate-crime legislation.

sources.title: Safety and security - Iceland travel advice - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Foreign travel advice for Iceland: safety and security. General travel advice, not trans-specific.

sources.title: Equality Complaints Committee | Ísland.is
sources.claim_summary: Official Icelandic government page on the Equality Complaints Committee: individuals and NGOs can refer Equality Act violations; the Committee issues binding written rulings; advisors at the Directorate of Equality provide support.

sources.title: The New Frontier: Trans Rights In Iceland – The Reykjavík Grapevine
sources.claim_summary: The Reykjavík Grapevine (Aug 2019): 'The New Frontier: Trans Rights in Iceland' - the old process (six paid psychiatric interviews, a year of 'living as your gender' before HRT/surgery) is being replaced by the informed-consent model, which Iceland has more or less legally adopted - the trans person is the authority on their own gender.
